name: server-data
title: Server Data
description: React hooks for a PageSource on TanStack Query, behind signatures of their own: useServerPage, useServerTotal, useServerInfinite, useServerQuery, useInvalidateSource, useSourceMutation and usePageController, with DataProvider and createDataClient for the defaults.
docs: `useServerPage(source, request)` loads one page with the query key `[...source.key, "page", filter, sort, position, size]`: the previous rows stay while the next page loads (`previous`), a superseded request is aborted through its signal, and it returns `items`, `status` (`pending`, `error`, `success`), `fetching`, `total`, `navigation`, `error` and `retry`. When the source has `fetchTotal`, `useServerTotal` counts beside it, a query of its own that never holds the rows back. `useServerInfinite(source, { filter, sort, size })` adds page after page (`loadMore`, `hasMore`, `loadingMore`) by page number or cursor. `useServerQuery(key, fetch, { enabled, staleTime, placeholder, keepPrevious })`, from `use-server-query`, loads one resource that isn't paged (a detail, a snapshot, a short list) and returns `data`, `status`, `fetching`, `previous`, `error` and `retry`; `fetch({ signal })` is aborted when the key changes or nothing reads it, and a key under the source's (`[...tasks.key, "detail", id]`) lets the hooks below reach it. `useInvalidateSource(source, { throwOnError })` refreshes everything under the source's key and resolves once the shown queries reloaded; with `throwOnError` (on the hook or per call) a failed reload rejects, for a toast. `useSourceMutation({ mutationFn, source, optimistic })` refreshes it once the change settles, and `optimistic: (items, variables) => items` shows the change at once and restores the rows if it fails. To write the server's answer instead of refreshing, `settleItems: (items, result, variables) => items` maps the rows of every page and infinite query under the key (totals stay) and `settle: (result, variables, current, queryKey) => data` writes every `useServerQuery` under it (`undefined` leaves one alone): each written query's read in flight is cancelled first, nothing is requested, and the rest of the key is marked stale (a read of it already in flight starts again). `usePageController(source, options)` keeps a `createPageController` for the component's life and follows the URL while mounted. The hooks use the app's `QueryClient` when one is provided; otherwise a shared default, so nothing has to be mounted. `DataProvider` provides one with `createDataClient` defaults when the app has none: two retries except on a 4xx (read from the error's `status`), 30 s fresh, no refetch on window focus. `createDataClient({ retry, retryDelay })` takes a number of retries (the 4xx rule stays) or a rule `(failures, error) => boolean`, and `isTransientError(error)` (a network TypeError, 408, 425, 429 or 5xx) writes the usual one: `retry: (failures, error) => failures < 3 && isTransientError(error)`; mutations never retry. Results reach React through TanStack's `notifyManager`, one `setTimeout(0)` after a query settles, so a test that awaits a single `act()` can see the state before it: call `notifyManager.setScheduler(queueMicrotask)` in the test setup, or wait with `findBy`/`waitFor`. With server rendering, mount a `DataProvider` per request. `useDelayedFlag(active, episode)` turns true once a load has taken 400 ms, for a status that says "Loading…" only when it matters, and `useReachEnd(onReach, enabled)` is a ref that runs `onReach` when an element scrolls into view, for infinite lists.
